findings.text: The first lede says plainly what Athena is, who it is for ("a lazy, one- or two-line request") and why it matters ("AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable"). A newcomer can answer 'what is this' within seconds.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The page explains why Athena's site opens with a study of a different project. Without this, the title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" would leave a newcomer unsure which product the site is about.
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit"

findings.text: A link to next steps sits in the header, so the newcomer does not have to scroll through the whole study to find out how to act.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself."

findings.text: The install path is concrete: prerequisites, clone, `./setup.sh`, then `athena ask "add a changelog"`. It does not say to run `athena ask` from inside the target repository, and it does not say what happens after Enter (a commit? a branch?).
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm"

findings.text: This header link speaks to the site's owner, not to a newcomer. A first-time reader may wonder whether they are expected to decide something.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Even the 'Start here' section quickly moves into exit codes, locks and teardown details. A newcomer who is judging Athena, not running firstmate, gets far more depth than they need, with no signal that they can stop reading.
findings.source: Start here: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: The state list shows only a name, a tag and citations. The reader has to look up each meaning in the lead-in or the Glossary.
findings.source: States of a piece of work: "queued initial"

findings.text: Several glossary entries (captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake, in scope) say the term is undefined. This is honest and shows Athena's care, but a newcomer is left with words they still cannot use.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call."

findings.text: Some transition cards pack several clauses into one sentence, which makes them hard to read on first contact.
findings.source: t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; ..."

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This shows the newcomer Athena's traceability rather than just asserting it.
findings.source: Next steps: "Check a statement: follow a bracketed claim id to the claim, then its source link to the file and lines in firstmate at the pinned commit."
